t: Japanese Government Bond (JGB): Overview, Examples
s: January 20, 2009 - The Bank of Japan implemented the yield curve control in 2016 in an effort to keep the yield on its ten-year JGB at zero and to steepen the yield curve. The yield curve steepens when the spread between short-term interest rates, which are negative in Japan, and long-term rates increase. The wider spread in interest rates creates opportunities to arbitrage profits, which is advantageous for banks in Japan. In 2021, the Bank of Japan reduced its bond-buying and began announcing purchases on a quarterly, rather than a monthly, schedule.
